title: Physiological Effects of Crunch: A Look at the Science
summary: GDC talk reviewing peer-reviewed research on crunch: cognitive decline past moderate hours, net productivity loss, health damage, and sleep loss as intoxication.

assertions.quote: once you get past 60 hours your cognitive function is actually worse than someone who wasn't working at all
the more fatigued someone is the more likely they are to make catastrophic errors

verdicts.note: Fatigue-error links are well documented; net negative team progress is a plausible extreme rather than a measured average.

Concludes long weekly and daily hours do not necessarily yield more output (the estimated marginal product of weekly hours turns negative around 63 h) and that fatigue raises the probability of errors, accidents and sickness; supports net-negative hours for physical piece work, programmer error rates not studied.

assertions.quote: a very clear linear relationship between hours worked above 8 a day or 40 a week with greater incidence of injury or illness

verdicts.note: Large epidemiological studies link long hours to injury, stroke and depression; stress biomarkers provide a mechanism.

Cites contemporary studies: NLSY workers on 12+ h days or 60+ h weeks had 37% and 23% higher injury hazard, nurses on shifts over 12 h or weeks over 40 h made more errors, interns crashed more after extended shifts; injury and illness supported, cardiovascular and mental-health effects not covered, and this is secondary citation not the paper's own data.

assertions.quote: there is a very mild negative correlation between working overtime and making a successful game

verdicts.note: The Gamasutra/IGDA survey analysis found this; it is a single self-reported dataset but no study shows crunch improving outcomes.

For munitions workers in 1916, hours reductions from wartime levels would have cost little or no output, and seven-day weeks produced about 10% less output than six-day weeks at the same hours; extra hours bought nothing, but product quality and software work were not measured.

assertions.quote: going without sleep it turns out physiologically is almost indistinguishable from drinking alcohol

verdicts.note: Dawson and Reid's equivalence studies and later work show sleep loss impairs performance like alcohol and degrades self-assessment.

assertions.quote: you reach caffeine tolerance shockingly quickly it takes about a week

verdicts.note: Tolerance to caffeine's alerting effects develops within days to a week in most studies, though partial benefits persist for some.

assertions.quote: allowing people flexible time over their schedules whether in crunch or not has basically nothing but positive effects

verdicts.note: Schedule control shows consistent positive associations in occupational health research, but effects are moderate and mostly observational.

assertions.quote: even after a full night's sleep and a full day off test subjects were not recovered all the way back to their baseline levels

verdicts.note: Shift-work recovery studies support incomplete recovery after one night; the size depends on the deficit.

assertions.quote: the cause of crunch is usually not uh is usually not a skill problem or a laziness problem it's an unrealistic schedule
